transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Since it is an induction hob, this tripping is usually caused by an earth leak in the power module or wiring rather than simple overload. It could also be moisture tracking under the glass if there have been recent spills. Please stop using the hob until a qualified engineer has inspected it, as repeated tripping indicates a genuine safety fault that resetting the breaker will not fix. You can safely check for any visible signs of burning or scorching around the control panel with the power off, but do not attempt to open or test the unit yourself.

reading.symptom: electrics in the house go off when using the hob

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hisense.
The fault they reported is: "electrics in the house go off when using the hob". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.
